#+TITLE: bisos_deb12-sysd --- Debian 12, Privileged, systemd, VNC/XFCE
#+OPTIONS: toc:nil

This leaf of [[https://github.com/bxObjects/bro_dockerfiles][bro_dockerfiles]] specifies the
=bisos_deb12-sysd= image: Debian 12 with systemd as PID 1, an XFCE desktop served over VNC and noVNC,
and sshd. It runs under docker as a *privileged* container. It is built =FROM= the confined image
=bisos_deb12-fresh:latest= of =../../../../confined/vnc/xfce/bisos_deb12-fresh=, which must be built
first.

A further instance of this image would be a sibling leaf with a numeric suffix
(=../bisos_deb12-sysd-2=): its own container name, host ports and cgroup v1 subnet in its
compose files, and no image of its own. See
=../../../../../13/privileged/vnc/xfce/bisos_deb13-sysd-2/= for one.

* Two Ways to Use This Leaf

This leaf can be used in two ways. Both build the same image, run the same container, and use the
same names and ports. They are kept at parity.

1. *With BISOS* --- through =./dockerProc.spcs=, a planted command of the =bisos.dockerProc= pip
   package. The leaf's path is its configuration. This is the path on BISOS platforms.
2. *Standalone* --- through =./imageBuild.sh= and =./containerManage.sh=. These need nothing but
   docker and compose: no BISOS, no pip install. They are the only way to use this image on hosts
   where BISOS cannot be installed (for example old RedHat VMs).

| Task                 | With BISOS (=./dockerProc.spcs -i ...=)  | Standalone                     |
|----------------------+------------------------------------------+--------------------------------|
| Build the image      | =containerProc_imageBuild=               | =./imageBuild.sh=              |
| Create the container | =containerProc_instanceUp= (also starts) | =./containerManage.sh create=  |
| Start                | =containerProc_instanceUp=               | =./containerManage.sh start=   |
| Stop                 | =containerProc_instanceDown=             | =./containerManage.sh stop=    |
| Restart              | =containerProc_instanceRestart=          | =./containerManage.sh restart= |
| Delete the container | =containerProc_instanceDelete=           | =./containerManage.sh delete=  |
| Status               | =containerProc_instanceStatus=           | =./containerManage.sh status=  |
| Verify               | =containerProc_instanceVerify=           | =./verify.sh=                  |

* Files in This Leaf

| File                      | Purpose                                                           |
|---------------------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------|
| =Dockerfile=              | The image: systemd as PID 1, the vncserver, novnc and sshd units. |
| =dockerConf/=             | systemd unit files copied into the image.                         |
| =docker-compose.yml=      | How to run the container on a *cgroup v2* host.                   |
| =docker-compose.cgv1.yml= | How to run the container on a *cgroup v1* host.                   |
| =imageBuild.sh=           | Standalone: build the image.                                      |
| =containerManage.sh=      | Standalone: create, start, stop, restart, delete the container.   |
| =verify.sh=               | Standalone: smoke-test a running container.                       |
| =dockerProc.spcs=         | With BISOS: the planted =bisos.dockerProc= command.               |

=imageBuild.sh= and =containerManage.sh= are the same files in every leaf of bro_dockerfiles. They
derive what they need from the leaf: its path (image name, engine), its =Dockerfile= (base image,
DockerHub name), and its compose or Quadlet file (container name, ports, subnet).

** The two compose files

A container with systemd as PID 1 needs the host's cgroup hierarchy, and that differs between cgroup
versions, so there is one compose file for each. They differ only in how cgroups are given to the
container:

- =docker-compose.yml= (cgroup v2): =cgroup: host= and =/sys/fs/cgroup= mounted read-write.
- =docker-compose.cgv1.yml= (cgroup v1): no =cgroup: host=; =/sys/fs/cgroup= mounted read-only with
  only its =systemd= subtree read-write. It also gives the container its own bridge network,
  =bisos_deb12_cgv1=, on an explicit subnet (=172.16.11.0/24=), for hosts whose default address pools are
  exhausted. That subnet must be free on the host and distinct from every other instance's.

Both name the image =bisos_deb12-sysd:latest= and the container =bisos_deb12-sysd=, run it
privileged, and publish the same host ports (see [[*Ports and Connecting][Ports and Connecting]]).
You do not pick one: =containerManage.sh= reads the host's cgroup version and uses the matching file.
To check a host by hand:

#+BEGIN_SRC bash
stat -fc %T /sys/fs/cgroup   # cgroup2fs: v2, docker-compose.yml; tmpfs: v1, docker-compose.cgv1.yml
#+END_SRC

* Standalone Usage

Requirements: docker, and compose --- either the =docker compose= plugin or the older =docker-compose=
binary. Both scripts refuse to run inside a container: run them on the host. Both can be run from any
directory.

** Building the image: =imageBuild.sh=

#+BEGIN_SRC bash
./imageBuild.sh            # local build (the default)
./imageBuild.sh -n         # local build, bypassing the layer cache
./imageBuild.sh -u         # local build, then also push the multi-arch image to DockerHub
#+END_SRC

The image is tagged =bisos_deb12-sysd:latest=. If its base, =bisos_deb12-fresh:latest=, is not in
docker's local store, the script stops and prints the command that builds it in the confined leaf.
=-u= pushes the image named by the =org.bisos.hubImage= and =org.bisos.hubTag= labels at the end of
the =Dockerfile=.

** Managing the container: =containerManage.sh=

#+BEGIN_SRC bash
./containerManage.sh [-n] <create|start|stop|restart|delete|status>
#+END_SRC

| Verb          | Does                                                         | Compose command            |
|---------------+--------------------------------------------------------------+----------------------------|
| =create=      | Create the container, not started.                           | =up --no-start --no-build= |
| =start=       | Start it.                                                    | =start=                    |
| =stop=        | Stop it. The container and its writable layer are kept.      | =stop=                     |
| =restart=     | Stop then start it.                                          | =restart=                  |
| =delete=      | Remove container + network. Writable layer lost, image kept. | =down=                     |
| =status=      | Show cgroup version, compose file, state and host ports.     | =ps=                       |
| =vncPassword= | =set= or =clear= the VNC password (see below).               | =cp=, =restart=            |

Before =create=, the script checks that the container does not already exist, that none of its host
ports is in use, that on cgroup v1 the compose network's subnet overlaps no other docker network and
no host route, and that the image has been built. If any check fails it reports every problem and
creates nothing. =create= never builds: building is =imageBuild.sh='s job.

=-n= is a dry run. The checks still run, but the commands that would change anything are printed,
not executed:

#+BEGIN_SRC bash
./containerManage.sh -n create
#+END_SRC

The container name, image, host ports and subnet are read from the selected compose file, so the
compose files stay the one place where they are set.

A first run:

#+BEGIN_SRC bash
( cd ../../../../confined/vnc/xfce/bisos_deb12-fresh && ./imageBuild.sh )   # base image, once
./imageBuild.sh
./containerManage.sh create
./containerManage.sh start
./verify.sh
#+END_SRC

** VNC password (optional)

VNC and noVNC have *no password by default*: convenient for local development, and nothing to
do. To require one for this instance:

#+BEGIN_SRC bash
./containerManage.sh vncPassword set      # asks twice; restarts the container if running
./containerManage.sh status               # shows "VNC auth: password"
./containerManage.sh vncPassword clear    # back to no password
#+END_SRC

VNC viewers and noVNC then ask for it. The password is kept in the container
(=/home/bystar/.config/bisosVncPasswd=), so it survives stop and restart and is lost on =delete=.
Only its first 8 characters count, and VNC traffic is not encrypted: across a network, use an SSH
tunnel. With BISOS the same is =containerProc_instanceVncPassword set= / =clear=.

* Ports and Connecting

| Service | Host port | Container port | Connect with                          |
|---------+-----------+----------------+---------------------------------------|
| SSH     |      2223 |             22 | =ssh -p 2223 <user>@localhost=        |
| VNC     |      5902 |           5901 | a VNC client at =localhost:5902=      |
| noVNC   |      6902 |           6901 | a browser at =http://localhost:6902/= |

The user is =bystar=, password =insecure= (the =USERNAME= and =PASSWD= =ARG=s of the confined
=Dockerfile=, inherited by the sysd images). Over VNC and noVNC the user is logged in already; the
password is needed for =sudo= and for SSH (it is not a VNC password: see above). A VNC client gives
a better experience than noVNC; with noVNC, copy and paste between host and container goes through
the clipboard of the noVNC side menu, and "Scaling Mode: Remote Resizing" in its settings makes the
desktop follow the browser window.

* Verifying: =verify.sh=

With the container running:

#+BEGIN_SRC bash
./verify.sh                                              # default container name and ports
./verify.sh bisos_deb12-sysd 2223 5902 6902              # explicit
#+END_SRC

It checks that systemd is PID 1, that the =vncserver=, =novnc= and =sshd-container= services are
active, that journald works, that the host ports listen and that noVNC answers over HTTP. It exits
non-zero if any check fails.

* With BISOS

On a BISOS platform with =bisos.dockerProc= installed, =./dockerProc.spcs= with no arguments lists its
commands for this leaf. =containerProc_instanceUp= makes the same checks as
=containerManage.sh create=. =bisos.dockerProc= supports cgroup v2 hosts only: on a cgroup v1
host its commands refuse to run, so use the standalone scripts there. See the =bisos.dockerProc=
README ([[https://github.com/bisos-pip/dockerProc]]).
